terms.meaning: A line at the top of a file that loads a tool or piece of code from elsewhere.
Dragging a list down to reload its contents.
A helper that sends requests from the app to the server and reads the replies.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the scrolling list, the pull-to-refresh control, a loading spinner, navigation, layout pieces, icons, shared styles, a shared card, and the API client that talks to the server.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup. The logic that uses these pieces is not in this packet.

sections.name: NotificationItem
sections.title: Shape of one notification
sections.what: Describes one notification as the screen uses it: an ID, type, title, body, a readable time, whether it has been read, and its icon and color.
sections.why: Keeps every notification in the list handled the same way.
sections.watch_out: The time is already turned into text such as 'Yesterday', so it cannot be sorted by date after this point.

sections.name: formatRelativeTime
sections.title: Turning a date into 'time ago' text
sections.what: Converts a timestamp into text such as 'Just now', '5 min ago', '2 hr ago', 'Yesterday' or '3 days ago'. If the date cannot be read, it shows 'Recently'.
sections.why: Likely reason: 'time ago' is easier to read than an exact timestamp.
sections.watch_out: The text is worked out once when the list loads, so the times do not update while the screen stays open.

sections.name: getIconAndColor
sections.title: Choosing an icon and color by type
sections.what: Picks an icon and color for each notification type, such as a warning for alerts and a trophy for achievements. Unknown types get a violet sparkles icon.
sections.why: Lets the user spot the kind of notification at a glance.
sections.watch_out: A new type sent by the server that is not listed here shows as a generic info item without any error.

sections.name: NotificationsScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Loading, refreshing and marking as read
sections.what: Loads the list from the server when the screen opens, supports pull-to-refresh, and marks one or all notifications as read. The change shows on screen before the server confirms it.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes taps feel instant.
sections.watch_out: If the server call fails, the item looks read on screen but stays unread on the server. The error is only written to the log, so the user is not told.

sections.name: NotificationsScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Header, list and empty message
sections.what: Draws the header with a back button and a Mark all read link, then the list. Unread items have a colored left bar and a dot. A spinner shows while loading, and a message shows when the list is empty.
sections.why: Shows unread items clearly so the user can see what needs attention.
sections.watch_out: Tapping any notification marks it as read, even if the user only wanted to look at it.

sections.name: NotificationsScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Closing the layout and styles
sections.what: Closes the list and empty-state blocks, adds a spacer at the bottom, and defines the look of the header, cards, icons, unread dot and text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the spacer keeps the last item from sitting under the bottom tab bar. Reason for the rest is not stated in the code.
